answer.rationale: With the line at 94% of committed volume and no buffer, delivery risk is the binding constraint, not just unit cost. memory_c2 shows the low-cost vendor cut cost sharply with quick onboarding, but it says nothing about lead-time reliability or performance under strain — a critical gap given zero slack in the line. Before ruling switch_primary_vendor in or out, I want the archived source for memory_c2 to see if delivery/quality risk was observed but omitted from the consolidated summary. Meanwhile, memory_c4 shows negotiating at renewal (using competitive benchmarks like the low-cost quote) recovered real margin and improved terms without a vendor transition, and memory_c1/c6 show incumbent renewals preserved integration stability and delivery continuity across cycles. Given the 14-day window and no room for onboarding disruption, negotiate_terms with the incumbent — using the low-cost quote as leverage — is the safer path to hit the 18% mandate while protecting delivery continuity. Switching outright is deferred pending verification; adding a second source or full deferral don't address the imminent contract expiration.
